given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)
given.why: Two loans are lent on 03-02, so each is due 03-16, and today is set to 03-17. Both are open and overdue. Only one day past due is tested, which is enough for 'before today'.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The database starts empty and the job runs once, so no loan has a reminder for today.

then.why: `fakeNotifications.sent` must have exactly two entries, so skipping the call would fail.
Each sent entry must carry the right `memberId`, `loanId` and `dueOn`.

then.part: then records a reminder for today
then.why: The `reminders` rows must be exactly the two loans with `sent_on` set to 2026-03-17. That is today, not the due date.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice, so loan1 has a reminder from the first run. It must have been sent only once.
loan2 is overdue by date and then returned. The test expects only loan1 to be sent.
No loan that is not yet overdue is set up. The two loans are both due 03-16 with today at 03-17, and copy-3 is added but never lent.

then.part: Sends nothing for that loan (already reminded today)
then.why: `sent` must equal exactly `[loan1]` after two runs, so a second send would fail.
`sent` must contain only loan1, so a send for the returned loan2 would fail.

then.part: Sends nothing for that loan (not yet overdue)
then.why: No not-yet-overdue loan exists in the test. A change that sends for loans due today or in the future, such as `<=`, would still pass.

given.why: `refuseFor(loan1, ...)` makes the fake refuse that loan.
B5's test shows that a failed connection becomes a `refused` result. The service treats it the same as any refusal.

then.why: The `reminders` table must contain only loan2's row.

then.part: logs `reminder.failed` at `warn` with `loanId` and the refusal's `error`
then.why: `toContainEqual` matches the exact level, event and fields, including the refusal reason text.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: The refused loan1 is lent first. loan2 must still be sent, so stopping the run at the first refusal would fail.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans are set up, two accepted and one refused, and the job runs through all of them.

then.why: The last log entry must equal level `info` and event `reminders.finished`.
The fields must be exactly `{ sent: 2, failed: 1 }`. The two counts differ, so a swap or a missing count would fail.

given.why: A reminder with a member, loan and due date is passed to `sendOverdueReminder`.

then.why: The recorded request must have method POST and pathname `/notifications`.

then.part: with JSON `{ memberId, template: loan-overdue, data: { loanId, dueOn } }`
then.why: The content-type and the whole body are matched exactly with `toEqual`.
Separate tests accept 202, 200 and 204, so a check for exactly 200 would fail.

then.part: any other answer ... as refused, with a reason naming the status
then.why: A 400 gives `refused` with a reason containing '400'.

then.part: a failed connection as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable
then.why: A network error gives `refused` with a reason containing 'unreachable'.
